Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Malik: Hey everyone, thanks for coming in. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the runbook draft. Jonah and Ava are with me from the technical team.
[00:08] Mara Chen: Hi, Mara here. Thanks, Sofia. We want to get the integration nailed down — LynxGrid product team is targetting a Jan pilot and marketplace listing right after.
[00:17] Raj Patel: Raj — big focus on private deploy into our VPCs. We have strict egress, and our security ops will want control of KMS keys and logs.
[00:24] Sofia Malik: Great, that's the scope — runbook + UAT sprint. Jonah, want to frame the proposed runbook sections?
[00:29] Jonah Park: Sure. My plan — top-level sections: pre-reqs (networks, IAM, quotas), packaging (helm chart vs operator, CRD design if operator), deployment steps (bootstrap, db/migrations if any, model artifacts placement), runtime config (batching, cache, quant profiles), security (KMS, mTLS, SSO mapping), monitoring & O11y (console dashboards, traces), and UAT checklist with smoke/perf tests.
[00:46] Elena Suarez: Quick Q — when you say model artifacts placement, are we talking S3 compatible storage or local PV? LynxGrid runs hybrid so we need both options.
[00:54] Jonah Park: Yes both — we should include S3 (or S3-compatible object store), plus NFS for on-prem. We'll show sample env vars for Redwood Private that point to either. Note: transcription sometimes calls it Redwood Private or redwood private, we have a few typos in automated notes.
[01:12] Ava Thompson: Also include KV cache warmup guidance — without priming we see ramp latencies. We'll capture cache priming scripts and a recommended warmup traffic pattern.
[01:21] Raj Patel: Good — I've seen big latency spikes when KV cache is cold. Can you also recommend default batch sizes? Our edge nodes will have variable sequence lengths.
[01:30] Jonah Park: We'll include suggested batch/latency tradeoff tables tuned to a 2–8 token-per-req mean and a small and large sequence profile. We'll also include how Redwood Optimize's recommendations can be applied automatically.
[01:42] Tom Li: On security — the important piece for us is KMS key control. We need to bring-your-own-key and HSM attestations if possible. What integration points do you offer?
[01:50] Ava Thompson: For Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM on the control plane side; for Dedicated we provide KMS integration patterns. We'll add a diagram in the runbook showing key flow: customer KMS -> encryption-at-rest for model artifacts and logs; and also explain envelope encryption for token caches. Note automated transcriptions sometimes say "KMS H S M" or similar.
[02:10] Mara Chen: Also SOC2 logging and audit trail — retention and schema matter for our compliance team. We'll need field mappings for audit logs to ingest into our SIEM.
[02:18] Jonah Park: We'll include sample audit log schema and recommended retention. For the marketplace listing specifically, we need a minimal set of docs: listing description, reference architecture diagram (one-page), quickstart steps, and a deployment manifest. LynxGrid will want the "single-click" flow, which is typically a Cloud Marketplace listing that launches a pre-configured deployment.
[02:36] Elena Suarez: For the single-click, do you support cloud marketplace deep-links that pre-populate parameters like region and VPC?
[02:42] Sofia Malik: Yes, in most marketplaces we can produce a pre-fill template; for private/air-gapped customers we'll provide a downloadable bundle with artifacts. For LynxGrid's hybrid customers we'll recommend the bundle + param store approach.
[02:54] Raj Patel: Network wise, our nodes sit behind a NAT and we have strict egress whitelisting. What endpoints must be allowed for the control plane?
[03:01] Jonah Park: We'll produce a minimal endpoints list. Roughly: control plane API endpoint(s), container image registries (if pulling images), metrics ingestion endpoints if using Redwood Console SaaS, and CRL/OCSP for cert validation. We'll include port/protocol table.
[03:15] Tom Li: And what about private telemetry? We cannot push PII out — can console be self-hosted or do you have an offline mode for logs?
[03:23] Ava Thompson: Console has a private deployment option where metrics and traces can be routed to a customer-managed endpoint or a VPC egress only. We can also ship logs into your SIEM via secure syslog or S3. We'll document the options.
[03:36] Mara Chen: On the operator vs helm debate — we prefer helm for simplicity but operator gives lifecycle management. What do you recommend for LynxGrid given our patch cycles?
[03:45] Jonah Park: If you expect frequent upgrades and custom CRD-managed rollouts (model swaps, automatic cache invalidation), operator simplifies that. Helm is quicker to start and easier to zone into marketplace single-click. We should offer both: a curated helm chart for marketplace and an operator bundle for customers who want richer lifecycle behaviors. We'll include both in the repo and show a diff in the runbook.
[04:05] Elena Suarez: Great. For UAT success criteria, can we define measurable pass/fail? We want to avoid vague statements.
[04:12] Sofia Malik: Absolutely — propose a UAT checklist: functional smoke (inference responses within schema, basic prompts), latency SLO (p50 < 80ms for small seq, p95 < 350ms across sample profile), throughput (sustained X req/s for node type), KV cache hit rate > 80% after warmup, and observability (dashboards populated and alerts created). We'll write exact queries to run.
[04:37] Raj Patel: Can we include a perf harness? It's easier for us to run a containerized load test with provided scripts.
[04:44] Jonah Park: We'll attach a perf harness repo link — a small container you can run that replays recorded requests at configurable QPS and sequence length distribution. We'll also include tooling to capture traces and token cost per-run.
[04:56] Tom Li: On data residency — some of our customers in EU require logs never leave EU. How flexible is region pinning?
[05:02] Ava Thompson: For Private we can pin to region and ensure control plane endpoints are in-region. For Dedicated we can also request a regional cluster. We'll add a section on region-residency patterns and recommended marketplace metadata flags.
[05:14] Mara Chen: Any gotchas with model quantization? Some on-prem boxes don't support certain kernels.
[05:19] Jonah Park: We'll list recommended variants per hardware family. The runbook will include a compatibility matrix: model variant -> required kernels -> hardware families. If kernel mismatch occurs we'll show how to fall back to a verified model SKU.
[05:33] Elena Suarez: What about upgrade/rollback? We need a canary plan if a model change causes regression.
[05:38] Jonah Park: Canary steps: create a canary route with 5% traffic to new model, monitor quality metrics (latency, error, and eval set scoring), and auto-rollback if score drops > 3% on core evals. We'll provide scripts to flip routes via the API and a short snippet for the deployment manifest.
[05:55] Sofia Malik: Let's call out stakeholders for the first pilot: Redwood SE (Jonah) owning runbook artifacts, Redwood Solutions (Ava) owning packaging and helm/operator bundles, LynxGrid DevOps (Raj) owning cluster prep, LynxGrid Security (Tom) owning KMS & audit approval, and LynxGrid PM (Elena) owning UAT acceptance.
[06:15] Raj Patel: Sounds good. A couple of smaller items: container image signing? Our registry requires images to be signed and scanned.
[06:22] Ava Thompson: We'll include instructions for image signing (cosign) and recommended scanning CI hooks. For marketplace listings we can provide signed images or instructions to pull from a verified registry.
[06:32] Mara Chen: Can you email a short one-pager we can hand to our procurement with high level SLA and pricing tier options for Dedicated vs Private?
[06:39] Sofia Malik: Yes — we'll include a pricing tier brief. Note that final pricing for Dedicated will need usage numbers; we'll start with a placeholder and then refine after pilot.
[06:47] Elena Suarez: One last question — any blockers on our side for the Jan pilot timeline? We need to know if resource constraints or approvals could delay us.
[06:54] Sofia Malik: The main blockers that would slow things down are: delayed access to the VPC/network diagrams, KMS approvals, and having a staging cluster that mirrors production network ACLs. If we get those quickly we can do the UAT in the week of Dec 29 as discussed.
[07:08] Mara Chen: We'll try to prioritize network docs and get them to you by Monday.
[07:13] Sofia Malik: Great. I'll recap next steps and owners in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[07:17] (meeting ends)
